projects.name: LA Outdoor Photo Shoot (34.05, -118.24)
projects.description:
Outdoor photo shoot near Los Angeles, CA (34.05, -118.24), later this week.

FORECAST (34.05, -118.24), retrieved this session:
- Today: 68°F, 5 mph SSW — Light Rain
- Tonight: 59°F, 0-5 mph SW — Light Rain
- Sunday: 68°F, 0-10 mph W — Light Rain Likely
- Sun Night: 56°F, 5 mph NNW — Mostly Clear
- Monday: 75°F, 5 mph W — Sunny
- Mon Night: 58°F, 0-5 mph NNW — Partly Cloudy
- Tuesday: 76°F, 0-5 mph WNW — Sunny
- Tue Night: 55°F, 5 mph NNW — Partly Cloudy

PLANNING IMPLICATION: Week starts wet (light rain through Sunday), then dries out and warms up Monday-Tuesday with full sun and light wind. Monday or Tuesday are the best shoot dates.

PLANNED WORK:
- Confirm shoot date (target Mon/Tue for clear weather)
- Prep gear for actual conditions on the chosen day
- Scout location and check golden-hour timing
- Capture and back up images on site

Tags: photography, outdoor, los-angeles, weather-dependent

tasks.name: Prepare gear for the forecast on shoot day
tasks.details:
Check the forecast again 24-48 hours before the shoot, then pack gear for the conditions that day. Forecast for 34.05, -118.24 as of today:

IF SHOOTING MONDAY OR TUESDAY (recommended — 75-76°F, sunny, wind 0-5 mph W/WNW):
- Polarizer and ND filters — harsh midday sun will blow out highlights; ND lets you keep a wide aperture
- Lens hood; expect bright contrast and some flare risk
- Light layers — warm daytime but evenings drop to 55-58°F in the hours after sunset
- Water and sun protection (hat, sunscreen) — advice tool flagged hydration
- Plan golden hour explicitly; sunset comes early, so scout the sun's path beforehand

IF SHOOTING TODAY OR SUNDAY (68°F, light rain / rain likely, wind up to 10 mph W):
- Rain cover or plastic bag for camera body; lens cloths and microfiber towels — moisture on glass will ruin shots
- Tripod with a weighted hook or sandbag; keep one hand on it in gusts
- Waterproof bag or shell for yourself; a light rain jacket keeps you shooting longer
- Lens hood as a rain shade; avoid swapping lenses in the open
- Reflected/overcast light is soft and even — good for portraits, so lean into it
- Backup plan: covered location (parking structure, colonnade, awning) if rain picks up

GENERAL:
- Extra batteries and cards; cold/damp drains batteries faster
- Verify tripod plate, remote shutter, and any gimbal are charged
- Pack a microclimate kit: lens pen, blower, dry silica pack

tasks.name: Lock in shoot date based on forecast
tasks.details:
Pick the shoot date against the forecast for 34.05, -118.24.

- Monday and Tuesday are the clear winners: 75°F and 76°F, sunny, wind only 0-5 mph W/WNW. Best light and lowest gear risk.
- Sunday is workable but wet: 68°F, "Light Rain Likely," wind up to 10 mph. Usable if you want soft overcast light for portraits, but plan for rain cover and a covered backup location.
- Today/tonight: light rain, 68°F/59°F — least attractive.
- Re-verify the forecast 24-48 hours out; this snapshot could shift.
- Once the date is set, note actual sunrise/sunset times so golden hour is scheduled precisely rather than guessed.

tasks.name: Scout location and confirm logistics
tasks.details:
Walk the LA-area location before the shoot day to sort logistics.

- Confirm parking, permits, and any access restrictions — many LA outdoor spots need a film permit for tripods or any pro-looking setup
- Identify 3-5 specific compositions rather than improvising on the day
- Note where the sun will be at your target hour; Monday/Tuesday are sunny, so hard shadows will track across the scene
- Identify a covered fallback spot in case the rain expected through Sunday lingers
- Check footing and tripod stability on any uneven or wet ground
- Save an offline map pin and arrival time; LA traffic means build in buffer
